instruction: Set the editor font size to 18 in VS Code settings.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened VS Code settings, used command palette to open Default Keybindings and keybindings.json, wrote a partial keybinding entry with incorrect 'when' clause, then lost focus browsing random files for remaining turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open VS Code command palette, navigate to settings UI, open and edit keybindings.json, type JSON content
metadata.failure_analysis: Model wrote 'when': 'listFocus' instead of 'listFocus && listSupportsFind'. After partial edit, got distracted browsing file system and opening unrelated Python files for 30+ turns.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a direct settings change (font size) which requires navigating VS Code settings - a capability the model demonstrated in the trajectory.
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing editor font size in VS Code settings.json. Evaluator uses official check_json_settings to verify the setting value.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (get_vscode_config) correctly opens VS Code command palette and fetches settings.json from the expected path.

Metric (check_json_settings) correctly handles the get_rule return format: expected['expected'] accesses {'editor.fontSize': 18} and iterates to verify each key-value pair exists in the actual settings.
Expected value {'editor.fontSize': 18} is semantically correct for the instruction 'Set the editor font size to 18'.
Single-step instruction is fully covered by a single evaluator check — no missing verification steps.
The static warning about type hint (str vs Dict) is a cosmetic annotation issue, not a logic error — the function works correctly with dict input at runtime.

rule_validation_issues.msg: metric check_json_settings second parameter type (str) may not match expected.rules type (Dict)
